1000.label: skip
1000.reason: This is a chapter overview section that explains the scope of Chapter 10 without stating any specific SNAP policy rules, verification standards, or casework procedures — it merely introduces what will be covered in subsequent sections.

1010.label: skip
1010.reason: This is a bare section header with no substantive content — just a title repeated with no additional procedures, rules, or policy guidance to compare against a caseworker manual.

1011.label: compare
1011.reason: This section establishes that income verification procedures vary by income source and type, and cross-references Chapter 7 for eligibility, budgeting, and reporting requirements. It defines the foundational principle that caseworkers must follow different verification procedures for different income types — a core casework policy that would appear in a caseworker manual.

1012.label: skip
1012.reason: This section describes the QC review process for determining whether caseworker income decisions were correct, not the casework policy itself for how to treat different income types.

1013.label: skip
1013.reason: This is a bare section header announcing that terminology definitions will follow, but contains no actual substantive content — no terms are defined in this section itself.

1013.1.label: compare
1013.1.reason: Section 1013.1 defines annualized income, a specific income averaging method caseworkers must apply when processing households with self-employment or contract income; it establishes which income types qualify for annualization and directs caseworkers to detailed procedures in Sections 1065.1 and 1065.2, making it a core policy rule for income treatment.

1013.2.label: compare
1013.2.reason: This section defines the policy rule for when anticipated income counts toward SNAP eligibility — it must be 'reasonably certain' — and specifies the caseworker's obligation to determine this on a case-by-case basis using household information and verification. This is a substantive eligibility rule that caseworkers must follow when processing cases.

1013.3.label: reference
1013.3.reason: This section is a terminology definition within the Terminology subsection (1013). It defines what 'averaged income' means for purposes of the handbook, rather than establishing a casework policy rule or verification standard that a caseworker guide must independently cover.

1013.4.label: compare
1013.4.reason: This section defines the specific mathematical conversion standards (4.3 multiplier for weekly, 2.15 for biweekly) that caseworkers must apply when processing income, making it a core policy rule about benefit calculation that belongs in a caseworker guide.

1013.5.label: reference
1013.5.reason: This section is a terminology definition within the Terminology subsection (1013). It defines what 'fluctuating income' means for purposes of the handbook, without establishing a policy rule that caseworkers must follow when processing cases. The actual policy for how to handle fluctuating income (averaging, verification, etc.) is covered in other sections; this section only provides the definitional term.

1013.6.label: reference
1013.6.reason: This section is a terminology definition providing the specific meaning of 'prorated income' as used throughout the handbook. It defines what the term means and gives examples, but does not establish a policy rule about how caseworkers must apply prorateion — that would appear in procedural sections.

1013.7.label: reference
1013.7.reason: This section is a terminology definition for 'Stable Income' — it provides a definition used throughout the income chapter but contains no policy rules, verification standards, or eligibility requirements that caseworkers apply when processing cases.

1020.label: compare
1020.reason: This section establishes verification standards for earned income that caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP cases. Verification requirements define what documentation is acceptable and what evidentiary thresholds apply—these are binding casework standards, not just audit procedures.

1020.1.label: compare
1020.1.reason: This section establishes an acceptable verification method for earned income that caseworkers may use; it defines what tools are available to verify income and thus represents a verification standard that caseworkers should know about when processing cases.

1021.label: compare
1021.reason: This section defines what counts as earned income (wages, salaries, tips, commissions) and establishes the verification and documentation requirements that caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP cases — both defining the policy rule and the verification standard caseworkers must meet.

1021.1.label: compare
1021.1.reason: This section specifies the verification procedures and evidentiary standards caseworkers must use when a household reports employment income — what information to obtain, what documents to collect, and what verification sources to use — which are binding caseworker requirements, not just QC review instructions.

1021.2.label: compare
1021.2.reason: This section defines the verification procedures and standards that caseworkers must follow when a household denies earned income — including what collateral contacts to pursue, what IEVS procedures apply, and what documentation is required — making these casework policy requirements, not just QC review mechanics.

1021.3.label: compare
1021.3.reason: This section specifies verification standards and procedures that caseworkers must follow when verifying earned income — including IEVS requirements, thresholds for further investigation ('no indication of information to the contrary'), and documentation standards. These are the verification methods and evidentiary rules that caseworkers apply when processing SNAP cases, not just what reviewers check during audits.

1022.label: compare
1022.reason: This section defines what constitutes self-employment income under SNAP policy (farming, rental property actively managed, roomer/boarder payments, independent contracting), specifies treatment rules (annualization, averaging, proration per Sections 1013 and 1065.1), and instructs caseworkers to ask households about self-employment — all of which are eligibility and benefit calculation rules that caseworkers must follow when processing cases.

1022.1.label: compare
1022.1.reason: This section specifies the verification standards and acceptable documents for self-employment income (tax returns, invoices, receipts, household statements) and requires reviewers to follow certification policy on allowable business expenses — both of which are verification requirements that caseworkers must meet when processing SNAP cases.

1022.2.label: skip
1022.2.reason: This section describes how QC reviewers should handle negative allegations of self-employment income during the audit process — specifically, which income to exclude from QC error calculations (Comparison I) and how to document reviewer acceptance of household claims. It is a QC review procedural standard, not a caseworker policy rule for processing SNAP cases.

1023.label: compare
1023.reason: This section defines what constitutes 'other earned income' for SNAP purposes and specifies which types of income caseworkers must count or verify, including training allowances and casual work — these are eligibility and income-counting rules that caseworkers must apply when determining household income.

1023.1.label: compare
1023.1.reason: This section specifies verification procedures and acceptable verification sources (receipts, collateral contacts) that caseworkers must follow when verifying other earned income — these are verification standards that define the policy requirement caseworkers must meet.

1023.2.label: compare
1023.2.reason: This section establishes the verification standard for other earned income claims: absent contradictory evidence, a caseworker may accept a household's statement of no such income. This evidentiary threshold is a policy rule that caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP applications and reviews, not just a QC review instruction.

1030.label: compare
1030.reason: This section establishes verification standards that caseworkers must follow when handling unearned government benefits — specifically, what questions to ask, what income items to inquire about, and the evidentiary threshold for accepting negative allegations ('in the context of its complete circumstances and history'). These are casework requirements, not just QC audit procedures. The reference to Section 512 further indicates that verification procedures applicable to caseworkers are being invoked.

1031.label: compare
1031.reason: This section specifies the verification standards and acceptable sources (SSA data exchange, award letters, correspondence, direct contact) that caseworkers must use when verifying RSDI income — these are the verification requirements that define how caseworkers process RSDI cases and must match what the state caseworker guide requires.

1032.label: skip
1032.reason: This section contains only a bare heading with no substantive text describing verification standards, policy rules, or caseworker requirements for handling veterans' benefits income.

1032.1.label: compare
1032.1.reason: This section specifies acceptable verification sources (VBA Award notice and direct contact with VBA) for veterans' benefits income, which establishes the verification standard that caseworkers must meet when processing SNAP cases.

1032.2.label: compare
1032.2.reason: This section establishes the verification standard for negative allegations of veterans' benefits — caseworkers must accept a household's statement without documentation if there is no contradictory evidence. This is a policy rule that caseworkers follow when processing SNAP cases, not merely a review instruction.

1033.label: compare
1033.reason: This section specifies the verification standards and acceptable sources (SSA data exchange system, award letters, SSA correspondence, direct contact) that caseworkers must use to verify SSI income — these are the verification requirements caseworkers follow when processing SNAP cases, not just what reviewers check.

1034.label: skip
1034.reason: This section is a bare header with no substantive content — just a title and category number repeated with no additional guidance, policy rules, or verification standards.

1034.1.label: compare
1034.1.reason: This section specifies acceptable verification sources for unemployment compensation income — the documents and contacts caseworkers must use to verify this income type. Verification standards are policy requirements that caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP cases.

1034.2.label: compare
1034.2.reason: This section establishes verification requirements for negative allegations of unemployment compensation by cross-referencing Section 512 (data matching requirements). Cross-references to other sections containing verification procedures or policy standards are classify as compare, since caseworkers must follow these verification standards when processing cases.

1035.label: skip
1035.reason: This section contains only a bare header with no substantive content — just the section title and reference number repeated. There is nothing to compare against the caseworker guide.

1035.1.label: compare
1035.1.reason: This section specifies acceptable verification sources and standards for Workers' Compensation income (award notice as best evidence; direct contact with WC office as alternative), which are verification requirements caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP cases.

1035.2.label: compare
1035.2.reason: This section cross-references Section 512 (data matching requirements), which establishes the verification standard caseworkers must use when a household denies receiving workers' compensation. Cross-references to other sections that contain policy or verification procedures are themselves policy-relevant and belong in a caseworker guide.

1036.label: compare
1036.reason: This section defines what constitutes 'other government benefits' for SNAP income purposes — a policy rule that caseworkers must apply when determining household income and eligibility. The enumerated examples (Black Lung Benefits, Railroad Retirement, USDA farmer payments) establish the scope of income types caseworkers must screen for and verify.

1036.1.label: compare
1036.1.reason: This section specifies the acceptable verification sources (award certificate, official correspondence, direct agency contact) that caseworkers must use when verifying other government benefits — these are verification standards that belong in a caseworker guide.

1036.2.label: compare
1036.2.reason: This section cross-references Section 512 for data matching requirements that apply to verification of other government benefits when a household denies receiving them; caseworkers must follow these requirements when processing SNAP cases.

1040.label: compare
1040.reason: This section heading indicates it contains verification standards for unearned income types other than government benefits — a caseworker must know what verification sources and methods are acceptable for each income type, as these standards define the verification requirements caseworkers must meet when processing SNAP cases.

1041.label: compare
1041.reason: This section defines what types of unearned income count as 'contributions/income-in-kind' (money from friends/family, alimony) — a policy classification that caseworkers must understand when determining household income eligibility and benefit amounts.

1041.1.label: compare
1041.1.reason: This section specifies verification standards for alimony payments (acceptable sources, document types, collateral contact procedures) and verification thresholds (e.g., 'denial may be accepted in the absence of evidence to the contrary'), which define the verification requirements caseworkers must meet when processing SNAP cases with alimony income.

1041.2.label: compare
1041.2.reason: This section defines what income-in-kind is and establishes the policy that it must be excluded from SNAP benefit calculations—a core eligibility rule that caseworkers must apply when calculating household income.

1042.label: compare
1042.reason: This section defines what deemed income is, how it must be verified (USCIS contact, case record review, sponsor documentation), and establishes the verification standard that caseworkers must follow when processing non-citizen cases — these are binding policy rules for casework, not just QC review procedures.

1043.label: compare
1043.reason: This section specifies the acceptable verification sources and methods for PA/GA income (contact with paying agency, screenshots, or official correspondence), which establishes the verification standard that caseworkers must meet when processing SNAP cases and determining eligibility.

1044.label: compare
1044.reason: This section defines what verification information caseworkers must obtain for educational grants, scholarships, and loans (the specific items to verify, acceptable sources, and allowable exclusions), which are policy rules that caseworkers must follow when determining countable income for SNAP eligibility.

1044.1.label: compare
1044.1.reason: This section specifies the verification sources and procedures that caseworkers must use when a household reports educational grants, scholarships, and loans — a policy rule about what constitutes acceptable verification and how to document it, which caseworkers must follow when processing cases.

1044.2.label: compare
1044.2.reason: This section establishes the verification standard for educational grants/scholarships/loans (contact school to verify receipt), which is a casework requirement — caseworkers must follow the same verification procedure when processing cases, not just when being reviewed.

1045.label: compare
1045.reason: This section establishes the verification standard that reviewers (and therefore caseworkers) must follow for other unearned income: they must verify both receipt and amount, and must explore all income sources. 1045.1.label: compare
1045.1.reason: This section defines the income treatment of foster care payments and specifies verification requirements (contacting the appropriate office, obtaining payment verification) that caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP cases with foster children or adults.

1045.2.label: compare
1045.2.reason: Section 1045.2 defines SNAP policy on how dividends and interest income must be counted, averaged, and reported — including specific rules about when interest is counted in which month, averaging procedures, and when household statements are sufficient versus when verification is required. These are caseworker eligibility and income-counting rules, not just QC review procedures.

1045.3.label: compare
1045.3.reason: This section defines SNAP policy on how rental income is counted (gross income minus business costs) and establishes verification requirements that caseworkers must follow when processing SNAP applications and recertifications.

1045.4.label: compare
1045.4.reason: This section defines what pensions and union benefits are, when they must be counted as income, and the verification procedures caseworkers must follow (referencing Section 1021.1 for acceptable verification sources). These are SNAP income rules that caseworkers need to know when processing cases.

1046.label: compare
1046.reason: This section defines TANF as a type of Public Assistance and notes state options for prospective vs. retrospective budgeting of TANF income—both are policy rules that caseworkers must apply when determining how to count TANF in household income calculations.

1050.label: compare
1050.reason: This section defines what child support income is, specifies verification standards (acceptable sources and verification procedures), and establishes the rules for handling positive and negative allegations — all of which are SNAP policy that caseworkers must follow when processing cases and determining income.

1060.label: skip
1060.reason: This section describes the QC review process for determining income variances — it instructs reviewers how to conduct audits and what procedures to follow when reviewing cases, not what caseworkers must do when processing SNAP applications or recertifications.

1061.label: compare
1061.reason: This section defines the fundamental SNAP eligibility income tests (gross and net income requirements) that caseworkers must apply when determining whether households qualify for benefits, including the categorical eligibility exception for elderly/disabled households.

1061.1.label: compare
1061.1.reason: This section defines the income eligibility test for prospectively eligible households—a core SNAP policy rule that caseworkers must apply when determining eligibility and that must be documented in a caseworker guide.

1061.2.label: compare
1061.2.reason: This section defines the income eligibility test for retrospectively eligible households — a fundamental SNAP policy rule that caseworkers must apply when determining and certifying SNAP eligibility, specifically which income month to use (budget month vs. sample month) and what constitutes meeting the income test.

1061.3.label: compare
1061.3.reason: This section defines categorical eligibility (CE) as an alternative path to SNAP eligibility that bypasses income tests, specifies what income tests are and are not required, and establishes the verification and allotment standards caseworkers must apply — all core policy rules that determine whether a household qualifies for benefits and what benefits they receive.

1062.label: compare
1062.reason: This section defines the $125 change reporting threshold for unearned income and specifies the procedures caseworkers must follow when processing unearned income—including how to handle prospectively vs. retrospectively budgeted cases, reporting requirements, and exclusionary time periods. These are core casework rules that caseworkers must implement when determining eligibility and benefits.

1062.1.label: skip
1062.1.reason: This section describes the QC review procedure for arranging and evaluating multiple income variances in chronological order to determine which to include in error calculations — it is about how reviewers conduct audits, not about SNAP income policy rules that caseworkers must follow.

1063.label: compare
1063.reason: This section defines the SNAP policy rules for how caseworkers must handle prospectively budgeted earned income when households are subject to $125 change reporting requirements—including what counts as a reportable change, how to treat averaged vs. non-averaged fluctuating income, how to handle vacation/sick pay, and what constitutes an interim change. These are core casework policies that DTA workers must follow when processing SNAP cases.

1063.1.label: compare
1063.1.reason: This section establishes the income verification and review procedures that caseworkers must follow when processing initial certifications and recertifications during the first and second effective months — specifically how to verify sample month income, correct worksheets for misapplied policy or computation errors, and determine which income figures to use in eligibility determinations. These are core casework standards, not just QC audit procedures.

1063.2.label: compare
1063.2.reason: This section specifies the procedures caseworkers must follow when reviewing and calculating income for the third effective month or later of a certification — including when to use verified vs. corrected income, the $125 threshold for income changes, how to determine fluctuating income, and which income amounts to use in benefit calculations. These are core casework rules, not just QC audit mechanics.

1063.3.label: compare
1063.3.reason: This section defines how caseworkers must treat unreported/unprocessed earned income sources—whether to annualize, prorate, exclude based on timing, or count actual sample month income. These are substantive SNAP policy rules about income treatment that caseworkers must follow when processing cases, not just QC review procedures.

1064.label: compare
1064.reason: This section defines the specific reporting requirements for earned income under status reporting (changes in source, hourly rate/salary, or employment status) and establishes the verification and variance determination procedures that caseworkers must follow when processing these cases.

1064.1.label: skip
1064.1.reason: This section describes QC review procedures for handling multiple income variances during audits — specifically how reviewers should chronologically order variances and determine which to include in error calculations. It is about the mechanics of conducting QC reviews, not about the casework policy rules that govern how caseworkers handle income reporting or calculate benefits.

1065.label: compare
1065.reason: This section defines how averaged income must be calculated and applied in SNAP budgeting — a core eligibility/benefit calculation rule that caseworkers must follow when processing cases with fluctuating earned income.

1065.1.label: compare
1065.1.reason: Section 1065.1 defines how self-employment income must be treated in SNAP budgeting — when to average over 12 months, when to prorate, and when no adjustment is needed. These are core eligibility/benefit calculation rules that caseworkers must follow when processing SE income, regardless of the QC review language used to present them.

1065.2.label: compare
1065.2.reason: This section defines the SNAP policy rule for how contract income must be averaged (over 12 months when earned in a shorter period), establishes when the averaging applies, and specifies the verification/correction standards caseworkers must follow — this is core income budgeting policy that a state caseworker guide must cover.

1065.3.label: compare
1065.3.reason: This section defines the SNAP policy rule for how educational income (scholarships, loans, grants) must be treated: after exclusions, it must be averaged over the period it is intended to cover and only counted when received or reasonably anticipated. Caseworkers must follow these averaging and proration rules when processing cases, making this a core policy requirement that belongs in a caseworker guide.

1066.label: compare
1066.reason: Section 1066 defines how to review and budget households with multiple income types (earned, unearned, annualized/prorated) and prescribes the procedures caseworkers must follow when processing such cases — including when to apply Comparison I and II tests and how to separately evaluate each income type. This is substantive SNAP budgeting policy that caseworker guides must cover.

1070.label: compare
1070.reason: This section describes how SNAP household composition affects income treatment — a core eligibility and budgeting rule that caseworkers must apply when determining benefits for households with ineligible members. The distinction between 'how income is handled varies depending upon the reason an individual is ineligible' is a policy rule caseworkers must follow.

1070.1.label: compare
1070.1.reason: Section 1070.1 defines how income from certain categories of ineligible household members (those disqualified for program violations, felony drug convictions, fleeing felony, or work sanctions) must be treated in SNAP eligibility calculations — specifically, that such income counts in full for the household while household size is reduced. This is a core eligibility rule that caseworkers must apply when processing cases.

1070.2.label: compare
1070.2.reason: This section specifies how to treat income from ineligible household members (prorating vs. counting entirely), which is a core SNAP eligibility rule that caseworkers must apply when processing cases with mixed-eligibility households.

1080.label: compare
1080.reason: This section describes how to handle SNAP benefit calculations when a household member's cash assistance from other means-tested programs is reduced or terminated due to non-compliance — specifically that SNAP allotments must not increase and may be reduced by up to 25% based on the reduced income. This is a benefit calculation rule that caseworkers must follow when processing cases.

1080.1.label: skip
1080.1.reason: This section describes the QC reviewer's procedural task — what records to examine and what determinations to make during a desk review — rather than defining the SNAP policy rule itself about non-compliance penalties. The policy rule (that penalties from other means-tested programs must be counted as income) is stated in Section 1080, but Section 1080.1 is purely about how reviewers conduct their audit procedure.

1080.2.label: skip
1080.2.reason: This section describes QC reviewer procedures for investigating penalties from other programs and challenging determinations — it is about how reviewers conduct audits, not about the SNAP policy rule itself (which is covered in Section 1080). Caseworkers do not need instructions on what reviewers may or may not challenge.

1080.3.label: skip
1080.3.reason: This section describes QC review procedures for examining state agency records and documenting findings about penalties — it instructs reviewers on what to verify and document during audits, not on the SNAP policy rule itself (which is covered in Section 1080). A caseworker guide would not need instructions on how to conduct QC verification.

1080.4.label: skip
1080.4.reason: This section defines what constitutes a QC variance for reviewer purposes — it specifies when a reviewer should cite an error in the QC audit process, not what caseworkers must do when processing cases.

1080.5.label: skip
1080.5.reason: This section describes how QC reviewers should identify, document, and calculate variances related to non-compliance penalties — it is entirely about the mechanics of conducting QC reviews, not about the SNAP policy rules caseworkers must follow when processing cases.

1080.6.label: skip
